summary.name: Copy 2FA
summary.one_liner: A free, open source macOS menu bar app that copies the newest two-factor authentication code from Apple Mail or Messages with a keyboard shortcut.
use_cases: Copy a 2FA code from an email without switching apps
Paste a texted verification code from Messages
Pick an older code from the last 10 minutes
Move Google Authenticator accounts into a Mac app
Keep one-time codes local with no internet access
summary.what_it_does: Copy 2FA is a macOS menu bar app. Pressing Control-Shift-C copies the newest 2FA code from email accounts added to Apple Mail, regardless of provider. It can also read texted codes from Messages if that option is enabled. The Recent Codes menu lists the last five codes from the past 10 minutes, with sender and source (Mail or Messages), and can be given its own shortcut. It can import Google Authenticator accounts through a transfer QR code and stores authenticator secrets in the keychain behind Touch ID. It runs in the App Sandbox with no network access and does not save the content it reads.
notable: Control-Shift-C copies the newest code from Apple Mail with no app switching
Recent Codes menu lists the last five codes from the past 10 minutes
Runs in the macOS App Sandbox with no network access
Imports Google Authenticator accounts via transfer QR code
caveats: Cannot read codes from Authy or Duo apps directly; Authy accounts must be set up again with a new QR code
Texted codes are only read if Messages support is turned on
